transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I came in because... my sleep is just all broken up right now. I get off my overnight shift and I'll just lie there in bed wide awake. And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I wake up scared. I just feel like I never even rested at all.
When you wake up scared, do you remember having a frightening dream?
No, not really. I mean... I don't remember dreaming about anything in particular. I just wake up and I'm already terrified, but there's no nightmare or anything that I can actually picture.
On days when you are not working overnight, are you able to sleep normally at night?

No, it's really the same. Like I was saying, my sleep is just completely broken up right now, no matter what time it is. Even on my nights off, I'll just lie there in the dark wide awake. And when I do finally manage to fall asleep, it's the exact same thing... I wake up scared, and I still feel like I haven't rested at all.
Do these frightened awakenings usually happen within the first few hours after you fall asleep?
I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't check the clock right away when it happens, so I don't know exactly how long I've been asleep. It just feels like... whenever I wake up, that's how I feel.
When you wake up frightened, are you fully awake and aware of your surroundings right away?

Yeah, I'm pretty much fully awake right away. Like I said, this is really why I came in... my sleep is just all broken up now. I'll get off an overnight shift and still just lie there wide awake. Then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared, and I'm instantly just... awake and aware of my room. But I feel like I never rested at all.
When you wake up frightened, do you ever scream, sit up, or move around?

No, I don't scream or anything like that. I just... I usually just open my eyes and I'm lying there. I might sit up eventually because I know I'm not going back to sleep, but I don't jump out of bed or thrash around. I just lie there feeling terrified.
The next morning, do you remember the frightened awakening clearly?

Yeah, I remember it. I remember waking up and just... feeling that awful panic. It's not like a fuzzy dream or anything, I know it happened. I just remember lying there in the dark, wide awake and scared.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent difficulty initiating and maintaining sleep with recurrent frightened awakenings and nonrestorative sleep, occurring on both work and nonwork nights. The presentation is most consistent with insomnia; shift-work sleep disorder, psychophysiological insomnia, and nightmare disorder were considered, but the symptoms are not limited to overnight work, no specific nightmares are recalled, and no parasomnia behaviors are described.

confirmed_symptoms: Lies awake for prolonged periods before falling asleep
Sleep is repeatedly broken up by awakenings
Wakes feeling frightened and immediately alert
Feels unrefreshed and as though sleep provided no rest
Awakenings are accompanied by intense fear or panic
Fully awake and aware of surroundings immediately after awakening
No remembered frightening dream or specific nightmare content
No screaming, thrashing, or other major motor behaviors

additional_requirements: Symptoms occur despite opportunity to sleep
Sleep disturbance occurs on both overnight-work days and nights off, reducing support for a purely shift-work-related disorder
